question: When a proper discrepancy route starts with a positive exact prefix gain but later loses at the tournament target, does its exact current-relative prefix gain usually turn non-positive early enough to stop material losing work, and does it rarely recover afterward?

relationship_to_prior_arm.evidence: The fresh proper-discrepancy screen was +19.5187 in aggregate but had only four positive seed blocks out of eight. Thirty-one local routes reached their equal-depth target; seven won and 24 retained the current path after 502121 total local-probe frames.
relationship_to_prior_arm.fixed_successor_if_supported: Stop a local discrepancy route at the first later authored-gap checkpoint whose exact cumulative axis loss is no better than the suspended incumbent through that same gap.
relationship_to_prior_arm.scope: This map changes telemetry only. It cannot establish the score effect of actually stopping, because stopping changes frontier timing and all later search.

instrument.behavior: Run the unchanged selective-axis-regret-catchup-proper-discrepancy policy and record exact authored-gap checkpoints on causal and local routes.
checkpoint_identity: route-local nodes and simulation frames consumed
suspended-prefix axis loss, route-prefix axis loss, and their exact gain
trust: checkpoint route identity must match exactly one completed probe result
gap, node, and frame counters must be monotone within each route and bounded by its result
local-route progress excludes the equal-depth target itself so a sign reversal is genuinely intermediate
candidate and retained-reference tracks, scores, and validity must be exactly identical

predeclared_map.seed_reuse_reason: These seeds and the prior live arm are deliberately reused only to characterize already-observed route mechanics. Score and validity movement are excluded from selection evidence.
predeclared_map.selection_rule: Build exactly the fixed sign-guard successor only if a first non-positive intermediate gain occurs on at least 12 local routes spanning at least six runs and both requested sources, no more than 10% of those routes recover to a strict target win, and at least 100000 measured local-probe frames occur after the first sign reversal. Otherwise close this guard without a live arm.
predeclared_map.next_step_if_selected: Implement one environment-selected proper-discrepancy sign-guard arm, prove its stop identity and one-action bounds in telemetry, and run a fresh focused 750k screen on actual seeds 120-127 before any catalog or canonical evaluation.
predeclared_map.non_claim: Observed work after a sign reversal is an upper-bound opportunity in the completed route, not a causal replay or a score estimate. The map cannot authorize promotion, canonical evaluation, or a multi-budget sweep.

result.decision: Close without a live sign-guard arm. Event breadth, run/source breadth, and measured-work gates pass, but two of 17 reversing routes recover to a strict target win (11.76%), above the prospectively fixed 10% ceiling.
result.interpretation: Intermediate prefix sign contains useful route-progress information, but a first-crossing stop is not clean enough: it would suppress observed winning routes. The next scheduler must add new categorical evidence, such as persistence or remaining-work context, and predeclare it independently rather than relax this fitted boundary.
